question:
study the diagram of the cross-section of a leaf given below. Which option shows the correct labelling?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7359c5f704b99158859349638508cc9d46a9378a0f470dbabbe9cae73e16298c.png]

options.text: a - upper epidermis, b - lower epidermis, c - guard cell, d - air spaces, e - chloroplast
a - upper epidermis, b - waxy cuticle, c - stoma, d - air spaces, e - chloroplast
a - upper epidermis, b - lower epidermis, c - stoma, d - air spaces, e - nucleus
a - waxy cuticle, b - upper epidermis, c - stoma, d - air spaces, e - nucleus

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The leaf cross-section diagram is labeled as follows: **a - upper epidermis, b - lower epidermis, c - guard cell, d - air spaces, e - chloroplast**, which matches Option 1.
 
• **Upper epidermis**: The topmost protective layer of the leaf, often covered by a waxy cuticle to prevent water loss.
 
• **Lower epidermis**: Contains stomata and guard cells, facilitating gas exchange.
 
• **Guard cells**: Specialized cells that regulate the opening and closing of stomata for gas exchange.
 
• **Air spaces**: Found in the spongy mesophyll, aiding in the diffusion of gases within the leaf.
 
• **Chloroplasts**: Organelles within mesophyll cells responsible for photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stomata:** Small openings in the lower epidermis allowing gas exchange (CO₂ in, O₂ out) and water vapor release during transpiration.
 
• **Mesophyll:** The middle layer of the leaf containing palisade and spongy cells with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
 
• **Waxy Cuticle:** A hydrophobic layer on the upper epidermis that reduces water loss and protects against pathogens.
 
• **Photosynthesis Process:** Chloroplasts absorb sunlight and convert it into glucose and oxygen through light-dependent and light-independent reactions.
 
• **Leaf Anatomy Functions:** The leaf is structured to maximize photosynthesis efficiency, gas exchange, and water regulation.
